item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00485","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C02","C11","C25"],"selected_candidate_label":"C02","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C02 plausibly supplied extensive, distinctive language and the core argumentative sequence of the later letter: a century of federal water-resource activity; repeated policy modification; resulting inconsistencies and piecemeal approaches; the need for a comprehensive review; creation of a water-resources policy body; recommendations to the President; designation of a chairman; and a December 1 reporting deadline. C11 is also a strong structural analogue for the Cabinet Committee format and may have contributed administrative framing, but C02 provides the clearest material drafting template. C25 contains the underlying commission machinery but is less textually and formally similar than C02.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"During the more than a century in which the Federal Government has played a vital part in the harnessing and development of water resources, our policies have been modified repeatedly to reflect changing needs and priorities.","parent_excerpt":"For more than a century, the Federal Government has played a vital role in harnessing our water resources... Over this period our water resources policies have been constantly modified and adjusted to meet the emerging needs of our complex and dynamic society.","explanation":"Distinctive near-parallel historical framing and policy-evolution language."},{"child_excerpt":"Unfortunately, we have often relied on piecemeal or stop-gap measures. In other instances the policies covering different Federal Agencies concerned with similar water resources have been inconsistent. Accordingly, it is both fitting and necessary for us to undertake a comprehensive review","parent_excerpt":"Frequently, new policies... have produced inconsistencies in our national water resources policies... piece-meal or partial approaches... tend to confuse... It is essential... that a comprehensive study and review be made","explanation":"The later directive closely reproduces the parent's problem diagnosis and transition to comprehensive review."},{"child_excerpt":"I am establishing a Cabinet Committee on Water Resources Policy. The committee shall undertake an extensive review of all aspects of water resources policy. Its recommendations... are to be submitted to me not later than December 1, 1954.","parent_excerpt":"I am creating... a temporary Water Resources Policy Commission... to study and to make recommendations to me on the policies... I am requesting the Commission to submit its final report to me not later than December 1, 1950.","explanation":"Same operative machinery—create a water-policy body, direct study and recommendations, and impose an identical month-and-day deadline adapted to a later year."},{"child_excerpt":"I am designating you the Chairman of the Cabinet Committee on Water Resources Policy.","parent_excerpt":"I am asking you to serve as chairman of this Commission.","explanation":"Parallel chairman-designation provision within the same letter structure."},{"child_excerpt":"The Commission on Organization of the Executive Branch of the Government, under the Chairmanship of former President Hoover, is undertaking a comprehensive study of water and power policies and organization.","parent_excerpt":"As you know, the Commission on the Organization of the Executive Branch of the Government has made a detailed and comprehensive study of the organizational issues involved in the water resources field.","explanation":"Both situate the new water-policy review in relation to the Hoover Commission's organizational work."}]}
